rules.definition: uses financial jargon or acronyms (APY, APR, FDIC, CD, compounding, variable rate, yield)
rules.rule: On a synthetic panel, jargon (APY, APR, FDIC) lowered appeal about 1.26 points on 1-10 (90% CI -1.38 to -0.75; 4 variants, 4 concepts); fragile.
rules.advice: Prefer plain words over acronyms where possible, but treat this as a tentative signal and test with real customers before making it a rule.

rules.definition: sells by saying what is NOT there (no fees, never, zero, without, don't)
rules.rule: On a synthetic panel, selling by absence (no fees, never, zero) lowered appeal about 0.55 points (90% CI -0.68 to -0.46; 8 variants, 6 concepts); fragile.
rules.advice: Try stating what customers get rather than what is missing, and confirm with real-audience testing since the finding is fragile.

rules.definition: frames the offer as avoiding a loss (stop losing, don't let X eat, miss out, before it's gone)
rules.rule: On a synthetic panel, loss framing (stop losing, miss out) lowered appeal about 0.73 points (90% CI -0.81 to -0.63; 14 variants, 10 concepts); fragile.
rules.advice: Lean toward gain-framed messages over loss or urgency framing, while validating with real customers before treating this as settled.

rules.definition: contains three or more separate numbers or percentages

rules.rule: On a synthetic panel, copy over about 22 words lowered appeal about 0.42 points (90% CI -0.53 to -0.08; 7 variants, 5 concepts); fragile, possibly small.
rules.advice: Aim for concise copy under roughly 22 words when practical, but the effect may be small, so verify with real-audience tests.

rules.definition: pressures the reader on time (today, now, limited time, act now, before rates drop)
